column2: One who chants thus the mantra of the lord of the night-lotus (Moon) with constancy soon obtains wealth, grain, sons, grandsons and good fortune.
Now I shall tell the Angaraka (Mars) mantra, granting wealth and sons: Om, with long vowel, "indu", "yuga", "vyoma", again with "indu"...
(coded syllables) — a six-syllable great mantra, giving Mars's grant of all desires.
Its sage is Virupaksha, metre Gayatri, deity Kuja (Mars). With the six mantra-syllables he should make the limbs and meditate on the son of the Earth.
He should remember the earth's son, born of Ishana's sweat, riding a ram, red-clothed and red-limbed, holding trident, spear, mace and boon in his hands.
He should chant the mantra a hundred thousand times, offer a tenth part with khadira fuel-sticks in the fire, and worship Kuja on the Shaiva seat.
Having first worshipped the limbs in a twenty-one-cell diagram: Mangala, Bhumiputra, Rinahartri (debt-remover), Dhanaprada (wealth-giver),
Sthirasana, Mahakaya, Sarvakarmavarodhaka, Lohita, Lohitaksha, Samaganam Kripakara,
Dharatmaja, Kuja, Bhauma, Bhumida, Bhuminandana, Angaraka, Mahisuna, Sarvarogapaharaka,
Vrishtikartri, Vrishtihartri, Sarvakaryarthasiddhida — thus twenty-one forms of the Earth's son are declared.
The mantra-knower should worship Mangala and the rest, placed in their own positions in order, and also Indra and the rest and Vajra and the rest; thus the mantra is perfected.
A doe-eyed woman wishing for a son should keep the Mars vow. The vow's start is praised in Margashirsha or Vaishakha.
Rising at the time of dawn, finishing the necessary duties, cleaning her teeth with apamarga, silent,
bathed, wearing red clothes, red garlands and ointments, she should prepare all offerings and materials red.
Having invited a fit Brahmin, she should worship Mars at his command, sitting on a red seat on ground plastered with red cow-dung.
Having sipped water, remembered place and time, and pronounced her desire, she should place the names Mangala and the rest on her own limbs:
on the face the benefactor of Sama-singers; on the nose and eyes Dharatmaja; Kuja (Bhauma) on the forehead;
Bhumida between the eyebrows; Bhuminandana on the head; Angaraka on the top-knot; Mahisuta on the whole body;
the remover of all disease on both arms; the maker of rain from the head to the feet — the wise one should place;
the remover of rain from the feet to the head; and at the end in the directions the giver of success in all affairs;
on the navel, heart and head Ara (Mars); on the face the Earth-born. Having so placed in her body, she should meditate on the Earth's son as before.
With mental offerings, having worshipped, she should place the arghya in a twenty-one-celled triangle on a copper plate.
Invoking Angaraka there, she should worship with red flowers and the like. Having first worshipped the limbs, she should worship Mangala and the rest.
In the twenty-one cells, the wheel of Mars and the Earth-born; having worshipped in the triangles, outside the eight Mothers,
then Indra and the rest and Vajra and the rest outside. Offering incense and lamps, she should offer wheat food.
In a copper vessel filled with pure water, putting red sandal, red flowers, rice grains and fruits, she should offer the arghya to Mangala; the mantra-knower should then read these two verses:

O son of the Earth, of great splendour, born of sweat of the Pinaka-bearer, I, wishing for a son, have come to you for refuge; accept the arghya, homage to you.
naradapuran:68:98	O one like red coral, like the hibiscus flower, O son of the Earth, of great fortune, accept the arghya, homage to you.
With the twenty-one names stated before, ending in "namah", preceded by Om, she should bow, and circumambulate as many times.
I bow to Mangala, born from the Earth's womb, bright as lightning, the youth with the spear in hand.
Then she should make three lines with khadira charcoal and, attentive, wipe them out with the left foot with these two mantras:

For the destruction of sorrow and misfortune and for the cause of a line of sons, I wipe out with my left foot these three lines I have made.
naradapuran:68:103	For the destruction of debt and sorrow, for the success of the mind's desired aims, I wipe out the three black lines born of three births.
Then, with a handful of flowers, she should praise the Earth's son, meditating on his lotus feet for the completeness of the worship:

Homage to you, remover of debt, destroyer of sorrow and poverty; O son of the Earth, be always the giver of good fortune and happiness to me.
naradapuran:68:106	Bright as heated gold, with a splendour like the young sun, giver of happiness, good fortune and wealth, destroyer of debt and poverty,
naradapuran:68:107	king of planets, homage to you, maker of all auspiciousness; show favour, lord of gods, vessel of all welfare.
naradapuran:68:108	Gods, demons, Gandharvas, Yakshas, demons and serpents all obtain welfare with desires always fulfilled;
naradapuran:68:109	by worshipping whom people in this world soon obtain happiness, homage to the son of the Earth.
naradapuran:68:110	He who, when moving crookedly, gives men sorrow, and when worshipped gives happiness and good fortune, homage to the Earth's son.
naradapuran:68:111	Homage to Mangala, shining in the sky, the cause of all welfare, the cause of wealth and progeny.
naradapuran:68:112	Show favour to me, O Bhauma, Mangala, giver of auspiciousness; O ram-rider, Rudra-natured, give me sons, wealth and fame.
Having thus praised, bowed and dismissed the Earth's son, she should give her own as she can and receive blessings.
Having given the fee to the teacher, she should eat what was offered to him.
Thus for a year on every Tuesday, then having made a golden (image) with sesame she should feed fifty Brahmins.
She should give a golden image of Mars to the teacher, having worshipped it in the pot in the diagram for success in having a son and good fortune.
Thus a woman devoted to the vow obtains fortunate sons; a man too should keep the vow for the destruction of debt and for wealth.
A Brahmin should chant the Vedic mantra "Agnir murdha..." Now I shall tell the Gayatri of Angaraka for the success of worship.
Angarakaya at the end of the word, he should say "vidmahe"; "Shaktihastaya", at the end of the letters "dhimahi";
Tan no Bhaumah prachodayat — this is the Gayatri of Mars; for the chanter it grants success in all desires.
This is the worship of Mars; now the Mercury mantra is told: ending in "pha", with ear and moon, Budha in the dative, ending in "ha"...
a six-syllable Mercury mantra; Brahma is declared its sage; metre Pankti; the deity is Mercury, giver of all desires to men.
The first seed, "namah" the power, application for obtaining all: "I always praise with devotion Budha, adorned with yellow garments,
his left hand on his knee, the other showing protection." Having meditated thus, the master of his senses should chant a thousand.
He should offer a tenth part with ghee and worship on the seat stated before; he should worship Budha with limbs, Mothers, directional guardians and weapons.
When the mantra is perfected, the mantra-knower should accomplish his own desires; he should chant it a thousand times daily for ten days,
and the affliction from planets is quickly destroyed, without doubt. The worship of Mercury is told; hear the worship of Jupiter.
The word Brihaspati in the dative, adorned with moon and other letters, ending in "namah"; it has eight syllables; Brahma is its sage;
the metre is Anushtubh, the deity is the teacher of the gods; the first is the seed, the heart is power; the limbs are made with long vowels, fire and moon.
Placing the left hand on a heap of jewels and scattering with the right, worshipped with yellow flowers, ornaments, ointments and garments,
he should remember the teacher of the gods, treasury of all learning, golden in lustre. He should chant a hundred thousand; a tenth with ghee or food should be offered.
He should worship on the Dharma-seat with limbs, directional guardians and weapons. When the mantra is perfected, he should accomplish his own desire.
In afflictions such as disease, in quarrels arising among kin, he should offer fuel-sticks of the peepal for their removal;
having offered for three days with night-flowers soaked in ghee, he soon gets two thousand garments and the earth.
The worship of the teacher is told; now hear that of Venus: "Give me cloth, to Shukra" — ending in two "tha", beginning with the fixed...
(coded) an eleven-syllable mantra; Brahma is its sage; the deity is the teacher of the demons; the seed is "dhruva", the power is Vasupriya.
With the earth-, moon-, fire-eyed syllables, the six limbs are made. He should remember Shukra, clad in white and anointed, giving wealth with one hand,
and with the left the posture of teaching. He should chant ten thousand and offer a tenth with ghee.
He should worship on the Dharma-seat with the limbs, Indra and the rest and their weapons; on Friday he should offer white sweet-smelling flowers.
The one who thus gets a garment and jewels twenty-one times... these mantras are always to be kept secret and not given to just anyone.
They should be given to a devoted disciple or to one's own son.
(Closing the sequence of 'union' syllables) — a twenty-six-syllable seat mantra: with this one should offer the seat.
Having conceived the form with the root mantra, invoking and worshipping in it, first having worshipped the limbs and on the filaments of the mantras;
on the petals in the directions east and so on, Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Pradyumna and Aniruddha; then in the corners the powers:
Shanti, Shri, Sarasvati and Rati, in order. They are gold, yellow, tamala-dark, and Indra-blue; clad in yellow;
four-armed, bearing conch, discus, mace and lotus; the powers are white, gold, cow-milk, and durva coloured.
At the petal tips one should worship the discus, conch, mace, lotus, Kaustubha, pestle, sword and forest-garland in order.
Red, hibiscus-yellow, gold, dark, black, white, silver, saffron: having worshipped, outside in front the lord of birds (Garuda).
On the two sides he should worship the conch and lotus treasures in order; in the west, pearl- and ruby-bright, the banner.
In the south-east the red Vighna; in the south-west the dark Arya; in the north-west Durga, dark; in the north-east the yellow general.
The wise one should worship outside the lords of the worlds with their weapons. He who thus worships the imperishable Vishnu with enclosures
enjoys all pleasures here and at the end goes to Vishnu's abode. For gaining fields, grain and gold, he should recall the dharana:
the goddess dark as durva leaf, holding a sheaf of rice; he should contemplate the goddess Bharati holding a lute and a book,
on the right of the God of gods, her face like the full moon, bright as the foam of the Milk Ocean, clad in white garments.
One who meditates on the supreme God together with Bharati becomes the knower of the Veda and its meaning, the best of knowers.
Meditating on himself as Narasimha, the god most terrible, having consecrated a weapon with the mantra, he returns having slain his enemies.
The practitioner, joining the mantra with the Narasimha seed, chanting a hundred and eight times, and with the left hand consecrating water,
sprinkling again and again; even one bitten by a serpent lives. Joined with the Garuda mantra, he should chant the five-syllable one.
For removing poison he should meditate on Vishnu riding Garuda. On an ashoka plank, drawing Tarkshya with ashoka...
worshipping the Lord in front with ashoka flowers, he should offer those flowers at the three twilights, seven leaves at a time.
The bird appears directly and grants the desired boon. Joined with the Ganapati mantra, he should chant a hundred thousand on a milk diet:
one sees the great god Ganapati directly here. Joined with the Vani seed, a man should practise it for six months:
he becomes a great poet and bewilders the whole world. Having offered pieces of guduchi, half a finger long,
mixed with curd, honey and ghee, the practitioner conquers death. On a Saturday, having touched the ashvattha tree properly with the hand,
chanting a hundred and eight times, he conquers untimely death in battle. Chanting twenty-five times and drinking water every morning,
he is freed from all sins, wise and free of disease. Setting up a pot by rule, filling it with pure water,
chanting ten thousand over it, the sprinkling with it destroys all disease. At an eclipse of moon or sun, having fasted, eight thousand,
touching ghee with brahmi and chanting, the best of practitioners should drink: he gains intelligence, poetic power and word-success, without doubt.
Offering ten thousand with bilva, he becomes a great lord of wealth. This is Narayana's mantra, best of all mantras,
the abode of all successes, told to you, Narada: "Narayanaya" — at the end of the word, he should say "vidmahe";
Vasudevaya in the dative, then "dhimahi"; "Tan no Vishnuh prachodayat".
This is called the Vishnu-Gayatri, destroyer of all sins. Om, heart, "Bhagavate", "Vasudevaya" in the dative:
the twelve-syllable great mantra, giver of enjoyment and liberation. It is for women and Shudras without Om; for the twice-born with Om.
Its sage is Prajapati, metre Gayatri, deity Vasudeva, seed "dhruva", power the heart.
With the syllables (moon, eye, Veda, five) all together the limbs are made: on the head, forehead, eyes, mouth, throat, arms, heart,
belly, navel, banner (organ), the two knees and two feet, he should place the mantra-syllables in order: this is called the placing of creation.
From heart to head is called the placing of preservation; from feet to head they know the placing of dissolution.
Then one should do the placing of the principles, hidden in all tantras: seed, breath, mind, heart-lotus, the disc of the sun,
the discs of moon and fire, then Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, then
Narayana, the discus: thus twelve principles. The root syllables, the heart-supreme, the Self, ending in the heart...
pronouncing the name at the principle, he should place in order on the head and the rest. The meditation is as before; the mantra's chanting is a hundred thousand.
A tenth part with sesame mixed in ghee for the offering. On the seat before, the mantra-knower, conceiving the form from the root,
invoking the Lord of gods there, should worship Vasudeva; having worshipped the limbs first, then Vasudeva and the others;
the powers Shanti and the rest in the directions and corners as before; in the third enclosure the twelve forms are to be worshipped.
Indra and the others with their weapons are to be worshipped in the earth's abode. Having thus worshipped the imperishable Vishnu with five enclosures,
one obtains all aims and at the end goes to Vishnu's abode. Of Vishnu named Purushottama there are four forms:
Trailokyamohana is told as first; Shrikara, Hrishikesha and Krishna is the fourth here.
Om, Kama, Rama, then in the dative: Purushottama. Armour and weapon with "agnipriya" at the end: a mantra with the form of fire and moon.
Brahma is the sage, Gayatri the metre, the deity is called Purushottama; the seed and power are in the love-abode.
With the earth-moon-one-taste-eye syllables, by divisions of the mantra's syllables, having made the limbs, he should meditate on Purushottama by rule:
bright as the rising sun, with conch, discus, mace and lotus in his shining hands, clothed in yellow — he should remember Shri Purushottama,
in a pavilion with shining arches studded with heaps of great gems, with a canopy resplendent with heaps of pearls, peace and self-control,
with the tinkling anklets of dancing divine women, on a dais of shining rubies, with brilliance like ten thousand suns,
adorned by the crown-tips of hosts of gods. He should chant the mantra nine hundred thousand times and offer a tenth part.
He should worship with blossomed lotuses on the Vaishnava seat stated before. Worshipping the Lord of gods so, he gains great prosperity,
sons, grandsons, fame, beauty, enjoyment and liberation. "Uttishtha" (rise), then "Shrikara", ending in "agnipriya";
of this eight-syllable mantra the sage is Vyasa, the metre Pankti; the deity is called Shrikara Hari, giver of all desires.
Bhishaya twice for the heart; "trasaya" twice for the head; "pramardaya" twice for the tuft; "pradhvamsaya" twice for the armour,
raksha twice for the weapon — all ending in "hum" are declared. On the head, eyes, throat, heart, navel,
thighs and shanks he should place the mantra-letters in order. Then he should perform the placing with the mantras told in the Purusha hymn:
on the mouth, "Brahmano 'sya mukham asit"; on the two arms, "Bahu rajanyah kritah";
on the two thighs, "Tad asya yad vaishyah"; on the two feet, "Padbhyam shudro ajayata."
He should then place discus, conch, mace and lotus on the finger-tips. Having done the placing thus, he should meditate in the pavilion as before,
on the god seated above Garuda on a red lotus seat, Shrikara in the form told before, bewildering the world.
Having meditated so, the practitioner should worship eight hundred thousand with a tenth part, with red lotuses and fuel-sticks of bilva and milk-trees,
offering each with milk-rice and ghee attentively. The ashvattha, udumbara, plaksha and banyan are held the milk-trees.
He should worship on the Vaishnava seat, conceiving the form from the root, the Lord together with limbs, enclosures, guardians and weapons.
When the mantra is perfected, he should perform the applications as before: Om, heart, Bhagavate, then "Varaha"
rupaya Bhur-bhuvah-svah ... "grant me kingship over the earth"...
This mantra, with the colour of Rama and fire, has Bhargava as its sage; the metre is Anushtubh, the deity declared as Adi-Varaha.
Ekadamshtraya for the heart; "Vyomolkaya" for the head; the tuft is "Tejodhipataye"; the armour "Vishvarupaya";
the weapon is "Mahadamshtraya": thus the five limbs are conceived; or with eight syllables divided by mountain-six-seven-arrow-Vasu,
the five limbs of the excellent mantra should be formed. Then he should meditate on the primal Varaha, bright as many suns,
Am, Hrim, golden below the knees and white above the navel, bearing in his hands boon, protection, mace, conch, discus, spear, sword and shield,
and on the tip of his tusk the earth shining. Having meditated thus, he should chant a hundred thousand and offer a tenth with lotuses,
soaked in honey, on the Vaishnava seat, as before. Conceiving the form from the root mantra, he should worship the Lord in it,
with limbs, enclosures, guardians, and weapons; for success of the yantra, by chanting, the god gives wealth, grain, land and prosperity.
In the month of Leo (Simha), on the eighth of the bright half, placing a pure stone in the five cow-products, touching it, he should chant ten thousand;
the practitioner, facing north, should inscribe that stone on the ground; he would ward off harm made by ghosts, spirits, serpents, thieves and the like.
On a Friday morning he should bring clay from the place to be accomplished, consecrated with the root mantra; he should divide it into three...
